images.title: Parallel lines after each fold
images.purpose: Show how the count of parallel lines grows 3, 5, 9 as a sheet is folded in half again and again.
images.composition: Three square sheets in a row with equal spacing and arrows between them, each with its count below.
exact_structure: Three squares of equal size with thin dark outlines, left to right, joined by two grey (#6B7280) arrows pointing right.
Square 1 (1 fold): 1 teal (#0072B2) horizontal crease at the middle; with the top and bottom edges that is 3 parallel lines, evenly spaced.
Square 2 (2 folds): 3 teal horizontal creases, evenly spaced; with the 2 edges that is 5 parallel lines.
Square 3 (3 folds): 7 teal horizontal creases, evenly spaced; with the 2 edges that is 9 parallel lines.
Under each square: the fold number and the count of parallel lines.
rejection: wrong number of creases in any square
a count label that does not match the creases drawn
images.takeaway: Each fold in half doubles the gaps, so the lines go 3, 5, 9.
images.description: Three squares folded once, twice and three times with 3, 5 and 9 parallel lines.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Students count the lines in each square and see the gaps double.

image_decisions.why: The three counts show the doubling pattern.
